source: Dog Aging Project HLES owner survey (42 behaviour items, 0-4), genotyped dogs >= 1 y
method: Per trait, owner answers are z-scored, signed and averaged into one score; a ridge regression on breed composition (stage-9 estimator, v2.3 panel) plus sex is fit on all Dog Aging Project adults. Accuracy is 5-fold held-out correlation with the owner score.

not_shipped.playfulness: held-out r 0.09: ancestry barely predicts it

stranger_friendliness.blurb: Relaxed and friendly with unfamiliar people, rather than fearful or reactive.

dog_friendliness.blurb: Calm around unfamiliar dogs, rather than fearful or reactive.

trainability.blurb: Responds to sit and stay, stays focused, walks without pulling.

energy.blurb: How energetic and active, day to day.

affection.blurb: Follows their people around and likes to sit close.

watchdog.blurb: Reacts to visitors at the door and people near the yard.

barking.blurb: How often they bark, including when left alone.

adaptability.display: Calm with noise and new things
adaptability.blurb: Unbothered by loud noises, new objects and new situations.

prey_chase.blurb: Urge to chase squirrels, birds and other small animals.

escaping.blurb: Tendency to slip out of the house or yard.

handling_sensitivity.blurb: Nervousness about nail trims and baths.

separation_distress.blurb: Restlessness, barking or scratching when alone.

resource_guarding.blurb: Growling or snapping when food or toys are taken away.

house_soiling.blurb: Urinating or defecating indoors, especially when alone.
